title: Cull components and pins as well as wires
scope: Schematic viewport rendering in Voltforge_UI. Full documents, simulation, routing and persistence keep every node and wire.

predecessor.note: Current committed PCB scene implementation and documentation were inspected. A later workspace cleanup removed the original root optimization backlog and UI-027 raw reports; this task does not recreate or revalidate them.

rootCause.detail: The component layer mapped the entire node-ID array although the wire layer already culled wires. Offscreen ComponentNodeWrapper, ComponentNode, pin shapes, hit regions, subscriptions and visual animation effects stayed mounted. Legacy schematic PCB pads also mapped all nodes.

implementation.change: Index conservative component bounds in 512-world-pixel cells. Include rotated bodies, external pins, text overhang, LED glow and sensor controls. Cache immutable node bounds weakly. Oversized shapes and very large view queries have bounded fallback paths.

Keep selected, dragged, wired and probed nodes, selected/bend-edit wire endpoints and the component owning an active pointer control resident. Native DOM capture protects controls that stop Konva bubbling. Preserve document stacking order.

Keep the visibility snapshot stable during drag-only geometry previews; a dragged component reads live coordinates from its own subscription. Other edits, additions/deletions and gesture completion update the index.

Mount only the visible component wrappers and their pins. Below 0.7 scale omit unreadable pin labels; keep pin hit targets and restore labels for hover, wiring, probes and retained interactions. Visible components retain their physical artwork and simulation controls.

Move sound transition ownership out of visual ComponentNode effects to one document subscription. Offscreen buzzer/button/switch/relay changes remain audible; panning does not restart sounds. Removal/editor teardown releases owned tone state.
Cull the legacy PCB pad layer with its components while retaining complete routing input. Expose mounted component and pin counts alongside existing wire/flow instrumentation.

acceptance.criterion: Mounted component/pin complexity follows viewport area rather than document size
acceptance.evidence: Both 500- and 1000-node fixtures mount 35 components/70 pins initially and 42 components after a distant pan; all nodes and wires remain stored.

acceptance.criterion: No lost wire endpoints, probe anchors or active drag targets at culling boundaries
checks: Native Stage drag mounts newly visible components before release without changing saved nodes/wires
Selected, dragged, probed and wiring-source components remain mounted offscreen
Distant zoom removes pin labels while retaining native wiring and hover hit targets
Wiring completes using full document geometry when its source is offscreen
Readonly pin probes stay usable, persist across culling, and cannot start wiring
A component drag remains live across culling and commits exactly one undoable move
Rotated external pins, spanning wires and dense breadboards survive viewport-edge culling
Offscreen runtime audio continues once, never restarts on pan, and stops on simulation stop/unmount
Nested sensor drag is retained by DOM capture even when it stops Konva event bubbling
Legacy PCB pads are culled with their components while full routing data remains available
PNG export still captures the visible scene after culling

acceptance.criterion: Pan/zoom stress p95 <=50 ms with at least 500 nodes, mostly offscreen

measurementMethod.build: Isolated production Vite build of the real CircuitCanvas
measurementMethod.document: Built-in resistor grid, 25 columns, 220x180 world-pixel spacing, connected adjacent nodes; normal load migration/routing is allowed to finish before measuring.
measurementMethod.inputs: 30 real mouse pan movements of 600px while held and 30 alternating real wheel events per size. Record input capture to last Konva layer draw, not physical monitor scanout.
measurementMethod.memory: One Runtime.getHeapUsage sample per size after HeapProfiler.collectGarbage; JS heap only, not total process/GPU memory.
measurementMethod.baselineCorrection: Initial diagnostic runs overlapped asynchronous legacy wire migration. Final before/after comparisons both wait for routingStatus=ready; those diagnostic timings are excluded.
measurementMethod.limitations: Single-machine samples; timing varies with host load. This does not assert a universal 16.7 ms frame budget or full live-app readiness.

visualComparison.note: Before/after production screenshots were also visually inspected. Other zoom/theme/DPI combinations are not covered by this equality check.

validation.detail: TypeScript, oxlint and all configured contract suites passed after the final implementation; includes 11 new component/audio assertions.
Production build and bundle boundaries/budgets pass.
Git reports expected Windows line-ending notices.

remainingWork.detail: Original UI-014 run failed development drag at 58 ms p95. UI-015 now passes all 9 existing drag checks at 47.2 ms p95, 79.8 ms max. Fresh baseline timing varied; this is scoped p95 acceptance, not a zero-lag guarantee.
Real-account application baseline is captured in VFOPT_X_001_APP_BASELINE.json. Seven follow-ups remain open, beginning with save-revision conflicts; this is not full application acceptance.

Visible large breadboards retain all physical pin hit targets. Raster memory, arbitrary custom components, extremely large scenes and all-visible workloads are not claimed to scale with this resistor fixture.

warnings: One pre-existing palette fixture Fast Refresh lint warning remains.
Two existing short-lived Vite SSR test servers emitted dependency-scan shutdown warnings; npm test exited successfully.
